mainTopic: Gentile children and זיבה impurity; the court that permitted gentile oil, conditional divorce, and the testimony of יוסי בן יועזר
overview: The amud opens by finishing a rule: a gentile boy of nine years and one day imparts זיבה impurity, and רבינא adds that a gentile girl of three years and one day does too. Next comes a story. רבי יהודה נשיאה tells his attendant רבי שמלאי that his court permitted gentile oil. רבי שמלאי suggests permitting bread as well, but רבי יהודה נשיאה fears being called a 'permissive court', like רבי יוסי בן יועזר, who was nicknamed for three lenient rulings. The other leniency of that court turns out to be letting a woman remarry when her husband gave a conditional גט and died within twelve months. The court relied on רבי יוסי's rule that the date on a document shows when it takes effect. רבי אלעזר asks an elder of that court when exactly she was allowed to remarry. אביי then explains which wordings of a conditional גט everyone agrees on, and which one רבי יהודה הנשיא and the חכמים argue about. Finally the גמרא returns to the testimony of יוסי בן יועזר and begins explaining what the איל קמצא is; this discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why a gentile boy imparts זיבה impurity
steps.stepSummary: A gentile boy who is old enough for relations is treated as a זב for impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since he is fit for relations, he also imparts impurity as a זב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining an earlier ruling: a gentile boy of nine years and one day makes things impure like a זב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The age is tied to when he is physically able to have relations. Once he reaches that age, the rabbinic decree that gentiles are treated like זבים applies to him.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit for relations, meaning old enough physically
The impurity of a זב, someone with an unusual bodily discharge

phrases.english: Since he is fit for intercourse,
phrases.notes: This is about the gentile boy of nine years and one day from the discussion just before this.

phrases.english: he also imparts impurity as a zav.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the reasoning from the previous daf about the age at which a gentile boy imparts זיבה impurity.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Being fit for relations is what makes a gentile boy impart זיבה impurity.

steps.title: רבינא extends the rule to a gentile girl
steps.stepSummary: רבינא rules that a gentile girl of three years and one day also imparts זיבה impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Therefore, a gentile girl who is three years and one day old is fit for relations, so she also imparts impurity as a זבה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא applies the same reasoning to a gentile girl, whose age of fitness for relations is three years and one day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason given for the boy was fitness for relations. רבינא points out that the same reason works for a girl at her own age.

keyTerms.meaning: Three years and one day, the age at which a girl is considered fit for relations

phrases.english: Ravina said: Therefore,
this gentile girl
who is three years and one day old,
since she is fit for intercourse,
she also imparts impurity as a zavah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a new conclusion from the reason given in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A gentile girl of three years and one day imparts זיבה impurity.

steps.title: Isn't רבינא's ruling obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבינא needed to say this, since it seems to follow directly from the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't that obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבינא: if the reason is fitness for relations, of course a girl who is fit is included, so why say it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a teaching is expected to add something new. If רבינא only repeats what the reason already tells us, his statement seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: It's obvious! The גמרא asking why something needed to be said

phrases.english: That's obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether רבינא's ruling in step 2 adds anything.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's statement about the gentile girl
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason of fitness for relations already covers the girl, so the statement seems unnecessary.

steps.title: A girl might have been treated differently
steps.stepSummary: One might have thought the decree applies only to a boy, who can draw others into sin, and not to a young girl, who cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: the boy knows how to entice others into sin, but the girl does not. So רבינא teaches us that she is included anyway.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבינא's ruling is needed, because without it we might have treated the girl differently from the boy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The decree that gentiles are like זבים was meant to keep Jews from mixing with them in a way that leads to sin. A nine-year-old boy can already draw others in, but a three-year-old girl cannot. Still, רבינא teaches that the girl imparts impurity too.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said; introduces a mistaken idea the teaching comes to block
To entice or draw others into sin
It teaches us (that the mistaken idea is wrong)

steps.whatToRemember: A gentile boy at nine years and one day and a gentile girl at three years and one day both impart זיבה impurity, even though only the boy can draw others into sin.

phrases.english: You might have said:
this one knows how to entice,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the nine-year-old boy. Literally, he knows how to get others used to sin.

phrases.english: but this one does not know how to entice?
It teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the ruling blocks a possible mistake
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the girl cannot draw others into sin, she might have been left out of the decree.
steps.terutzMaskana: The girl imparts זיבה impurity just like the boy.

steps.title: רבי יהודה נשיאה tells רבי שמלאי that gentile oil was permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a story in which רבי יהודה נשיאה tells his attendant that his court permitted gentile oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה נשיאה was walking while leaning on the shoulder of his attendant רבי שמלאי. He said to him: שמלאי, you were not in the בית מדרש last night when we permitted the oil.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a story. רבי יהודה נשיאה tells his attendant that his court permitted the oil of gentiles.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Gentile oil had been forbidden by an earlier decree. Here the court of רבי יהודה נשיאה reports that it has lifted that ban, which leads into a discussion of whether more could be permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Oil, here oil made by gentiles

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source that the ban on gentile oil was lifted by the court of רבי יהודה נשיאה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda Nesia was walking while leaning
on the shoulder of Rabbi Simlai, his attendant.
He said to him: Simlai,
you were not in the study hall last night
when we permitted the oil.
phrases.notes: He means oil of gentiles, which had been forbidden until then.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the story of permitting gentile oil.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The court of רבי יהודה נשיאה permitted gentile oil.

steps.title: רבי שמלאי suggests permitting bread too
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמלאי says that in their days the court will also permit gentile bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: In our days, you will permit bread as well!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמלאי responds by suggesting that the court go further and also permit gentile bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since one gentile food decree was just lifted, רבי שמלאי suggests that the bread decree could be lifted too. This sets up רבי יהודה נשיאה's worry in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Bread, here bread baked by gentiles

phrases.english: He said to him: In our days
you will permit bread as well!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: בְּיָמֵינוּ תַּתִּיר אַף אֶת הַפַּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the news in step 5 by proposing another leniency.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A suggestion that gentile bread should also be permitted.

steps.title: The worry about being called a permissive court
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה נשיאה turns down the idea, worried people will call his court permissive.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If so, people will call us 'the permissive court'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה נשיאה pushes back: permitting bread as well would make his court look too lenient.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His objection is about reputation, not about whether bread itself could be permitted. He backs up this worry with a משנה in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The court that permits, a permissive court

phrases.english: He said to him: If so,
they will call us 'the permissive court'!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: אִם כֵּן קָרוּ לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion in step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proposal to permit gentile bread
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Too many leniencies would give the court a reputation for being permissive.

steps.title: The משנה about רבי יוסי בן יועזר, 'the Permitter'
steps.stepSummary: A משנה shows that רבי יוסי בן יועזר was nicknamed 'the Permitter' because of three rulings.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: רבי יוסי בן יועזר of צרידה testified that the איל קמצא locust is kosher, that the liquids of the slaughterhouse are pure, and that one who touches a dead body is impure. And they called him 'יוסף שריא', 'the Permitter.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה נשיאה brings a משנה to show that a rabbi could get a lenient nickname because of his rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי בן יועזר gave three rulings and earned the name 'the Permitter.' This shows the worry in step 7 is real. The third ruling sounds strict, and the גמרא explains it later.

keyTerms.meaning: He testified about a law he had received
Liquids of the slaughterhouse in the בית המקדש

steps.confusionAlert: 'One who touches a dead body is impure' sounds like a strict ruling, not a lenient one. Don't get stuck. The גמרא will explain soon how this counts as a leniency.

phrases.english: As we learned in a Mishnah:

phrases.aramaic: הֵעִיד רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן יוֹעֶזֶר אִישׁ צְרֵידָה
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei ben Yo'ezer of Tzereida testified
about the eil kamtza locust, that it is kosher,
and about the liquids of the slaughterhouse, that they are pure,
phrases.notes: This is the slaughtering area in the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: and about one who touches a dead body, that he is impure,
and they called him 'Yosef the Permitter.'
phrases.notes: יוסף here is just another form of the name יוסי.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: הֵעִיד רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן יוֹעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the worry raised in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That lenient rulings can earn a court a 'permissive' reputation
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in עדיות about רבי יוסי בן יועזר

steps.title: רבי שמלאי: two leniencies are not like three
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמלאי answers that רבי יוסי בן יועזר permitted three things, while the court would have only two.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There, he permitted three things, and the Master permitted one. Even if the Master permits one more, it is still only two!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמלאי argues the comparison doesn't fit: permitting oil and bread makes only two leniencies, not three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The nickname in the משנה came after three lenient rulings. Two rulings would not reach that level, so the worry about reputation does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master, a respectful way to say 'you'

phrases.english: He said to him: There, he permitted three,
and the Master permitted one,
and if the Master permits one more,
it is still only two!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back against the proof brought in step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The use of the משנה as a reason not to permit bread
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The nickname came after three leniencies. Oil and bread together make only two.

steps.title: רבי יהודה נשיאה already permitted something else
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה נשיאה replies that he already permitted another thing, so bread would make three.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I have also already permitted another thing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה נשיאה answers that the count is already two, so adding bread would bring it to three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This brings back his worry: with oil, the other ruling, and bread, there would be three leniencies, just like רבי יוסי בן יועזר.

phrases.english: He said to him: I [also] permitted another.
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא נָמֵי שְׁרַאי אַחֲרִיתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי שמלאי's count in step 9.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Permitting bread would bring the total to only two.
steps.terutzMaskana: There is already a second leniency, so bread would be the third.

steps.title: What was the other leniency?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what other thing רבי יהודה נשיאה permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which other leniency he meant. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story mentions another ruling without naming it. The גמרא stops to find out what it was.

phrases.english: What is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the details of the leniency mentioned in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which other matter רבי יהודה נשיאה permitted

steps.title: The other leniency: the conditional divorce case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the other thing the court permitted was a woman whose husband gave her a conditional גט and died before the deadline.
steps.simpleTranslation: A משנה teaches: If a man says, 'This is your גט if I don't come back within twelve months,' and he dies within the twelve months, it is not a גט. A ברייתא on that משנה says: 'Our Rabbis permitted her to marry.' We asked: who are 'our Rabbis'? רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: it is the court that permitted oil.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 11. It shows the other leniency of רבי יהודה נשיאה's court: they let a woman remarry in a conditional-divorce case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the plain משנה, the גט fails because the husband died before the condition was met, and a גט cannot work after death. Even so, a ברייתא says 'our Rabbis' allowed her to remarry. שמואל identifies those Rabbis as the same court that permitted oil, so that court already had one more leniency. This backs up רבי יהודה נשיאה's claim in Step 10 that permitting bread would make three.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught about it (about this משנה)
'Our Rabbis', here meaning a specific later court

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna: This is your bill of divorce
if I do not come back from now
until twelve months,
and he died within the twelve months
it is not a bill of divorce,
and it was taught about it:
and our Rabbis permitted her to marry,
and we asked: who are 'our Rabbis'?
Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The court that permitted the oil.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: זֶה גִּיטִּיךְ אִם לֹא בָּאתִי מִכָּאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of Step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The court also permitted a woman to remarry in the case of a conditional גט where the husband died within twelve months.
steps.whyThisMatters: It confirms that the court would have three leniencies (oil, the גט case, and bread), matching the three of רבי יוסי בן יועזר.

steps.title: The court's reasoning: the date on the document
steps.stepSummary: The court followed רבי יוסי, who holds that the date written on a document shows when it takes effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: They hold like רבי יוסי, who said: the date written on a document proves when it takes effect.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the court let the woman remarry, even though the משנה says the גט is not valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי holds that a document counts from the date written on it. So even without the word 'from now', the גט works back to the day it was dated, which was before the husband died. That is why it is not a case of a גט taking effect after death.

keyTerms.meaning: The date written on a document
Proves about it (shows when it takes effect)

phrases.english: They hold in accordance with Rabbi Yosei,
who said: The date of a document
proves about it.
phrases.notes: He means the גט counts from the date written on it, which is before the husband died.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the court's ruling from Step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The court followed רבי יוסי: a document's date shows when it takes effect, so the conditional גט works retroactively from its date.

steps.title: רבי יהודה הנשיא once ruled the same way
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא reports that רבי יהודה הנשיא had once ruled this way, but the חכמים did not agree with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא, son of רבי חייא בר אבא, said: רבי יהודה הנשיא ruled this way, and they did not agree with him his whole lifetime. Some say: all his colleagues did not agree with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a historical note: this leniency had been ruled before, but back then it was not accepted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling of רבי יהודה נשיאה's court was not brand new. רבי יהודה הנשיא had already said it, but nobody accepted it in his time. There are two versions of the wording: 'all his lifetime' (שעתו) or 'all his colleagues' (סיעתו).

phrases.english: And Rabbi Abba said,
son of Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba:
Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi ruled this way,
and they did not agree with him his entire lifetime,
and some say: all of his colleagues.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds background on the history of the ruling explained in Step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: This leniency was first ruled by רבי יהודה הנשיא but was not accepted in his time (or by his colleagues).

steps.title: When was the woman allowed to remarry?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר asks an elder of the court whether they permitted the woman right away or only after twelve months.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said to a certain elder: When you permitted her, did you permit her right away, since the husband is surely not coming back? Or perhaps only after twelve months, because only then was his condition fulfilled?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר asks a practical question about the court's ruling: at what point could the woman actually remarry?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the husband is dead, it is certain he won't come back, so maybe she can remarry right away. On the other hand, the condition was 'if I don't come within twelve months', so maybe it is only fulfilled when the twelve months are over. The question is whether a condition counts as met because we know the result, or only once the time has actually passed.

keyTerms.meaning: An elder (here, a member of that court)

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said
phrases.notes: Some versions say אליעזר, in round brackets. The corrected wording is אלעזר, in square brackets.

phrases.english: to a certain elder:
When you permitted her,
did you permit her immediately,
since he is not coming back,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא לְאַחַר שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חוֹדֶשׁ,
phrases.english: or perhaps only after twelve months,
because only then was his condition fulfilled?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks a follow-up question about how the court's ruling worked in practice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the woman may remarry immediately after the husband's death or only once the twelve months pass.

steps.title: The elder points to the same question in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The elder replies that the same question can be asked about the next case in the משנה, where the husband said 'from now'.
steps.simpleTranslation: You could ask the same question about the משנה. We learned: 'This is your גט from now if I don't come back within twelve months,' and he died within the twelve months: it is a גט, because his condition was fulfilled.
steps.whatsHappening: The elder doesn't answer directly. He shows that רבי אלעזר's question applies to an accepted case in the משנה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the 'from now' case everyone agrees the גט is valid, yet we still need to know when she may remarry: right away or after twelve months. So the question is not special to the court's leniency; it already comes up in the משנה. The elder is challenging why רבי אלעזר asks him about the court at all, and רבי אלעזר answers this in step 18.

keyTerms.meaning: Then you should ask it (also) about
From now (the גט takes effect immediately)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. Without 'from now', the משנה says it is not a גט. With 'from now', it is a גט. The elder is pointing to the second case.

phrases.english: Then you should ask this about the mishna too,
phrases.notes: This is the elder speaking back to רבי אלעזר.

phrases.english: as we learned: 'This is your bill of divorce from now

phrases.aramaic: אִם לֹא בָּאתִי מִכָּאן עַד שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חוֹדֶשׁ״,
phrases.english: if I do not come back from now until twelve months,'
and he died within the twelve months
it is a bill of divorce,
because his condition was fulfilled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רבי אלעזר's question by moving it onto the 'from now' case of the משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The question isn't unique to the court's ruling; it applies equally to the משנה's 'from now' case, which is a valid גט.

steps.title: The elder: you could ask the same question about the משנה itself
steps.stepSummary: The elder spells out the question: in the משנה's case, is the גט valid immediately because the husband will never come back, or only after twelve months when the condition is complete?
steps.simpleTranslation: And you could ask this question here too: Is the גט valid right away, since the husband is certainly not coming? Or maybe only after twelve months, since only then is his condition fulfilled?
steps.whatsHappening: The elder pushes back on רבי אלעזר. He says the 'right away or after twelve months' question is not special to the court's ruling; it comes up in the משנה too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the husband dies, we know he will never come back, so in one sense the condition is already settled. But technically the condition was 'if I don't come within twelve months', and that time has not finished yet. The elder is saying: this doubt exists in the משנה's own case, so why ask me about the court?

phrases.english: And let the question be raised for you:
phrases.notes: He means: you could ask this same doubt about the משנה's case, not just about the court.

phrases.english: Is it a valid divorce immediately,
since he is certainly not coming back,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִּלְמָא לְאַחַר שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חוֹדֶשׁ,
phrases.english: or perhaps only after twelve months,
since only then is his condition fulfilled?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the elder's reply from step 16 by stating the exact doubt as it applies to the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's choice to ask the elder about the court's ruling
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same doubt arises in the משנה's own case, so the question is not really about what the court did.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: true, but you were there
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר agrees the question applies to the משנה too, but says he asked the elder because the elder was present at that court session.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is true. But I asked you because you were part of that gathering.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the elder's pushback. He admits the question is general, but he wanted a firsthand report of what the court actually did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Asking about the משנה would only lead to logical guesswork. Asking someone who was there gives a real answer about how the court ruled in practice. That is why רבי אלעזר went to the elder.

keyTerms.meaning: Assembly, the counted group of judges

phrases.english: Yes, it is indeed so;
but I asked you because you were at that assembly.
phrases.notes: The words 'I asked you' are not written out; the גמרא assumes them. 'That assembly' is the court of רבי יהודה נשיאה, which permitted the oil.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין הָכִי נָמֵי, אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם דַּהֲוֵית בְּהָהוּא מִנְיָינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the elder's pushback in step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Concedes the point but explains the real reason for the question
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אלעזר's question seemed out of place, since it applies equally to the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The question is general, but he asked an eyewitness to learn what the court actually ruled.

steps.title: אביי: everyone agrees about 'when the sun comes out'
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that if the husband said the גט works 'when the sun comes out of its sheath' and he died at night, all agree it is an invalid גט after death.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי says: Everyone agrees that if he said 'when the sun comes out of its sheath', he means the גט starts when the sun comes out. So if he dies during the night, it is a גט after death.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי begins mapping out where רבי יהודה הנשיא and the חכמים agree and where they argue. This first wording is a case where everyone agrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'When' sets a starting time: the גט only begins to work at sunrise. If the husband is already dead by then, the גט would start after his death. A גט cannot take effect after death, so it does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: Its sheath, a picture of the sun rising
A גט that would only take effect after death, which is invalid

phrases.english: Abaye says:
All agree
that if he said 'When the sun comes out of its sheath,'
phrases.notes: 'Comes out of its sheath' is just a way of saying sunrise.

phrases.english: he is telling her it works once the sun comes out,
and if he dies during the night,
it is a divorce after death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the story about the court to אביי's explanation of exactly where רבי יהודה הנשיא and the חכמים argue.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wording of 'when X happens' makes the גט start only at that time, so if he dies first it is invalid according to everyone.

steps.title: Everyone agrees 'on condition that' works backward from now
steps.stepSummary: If he said 'on condition that the sun comes out', it is a גט from now with a condition, so even if he dies at night the גט is valid from while he was alive. This follows רב הונא's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said 'on condition that the sun comes out of its sheath', he is telling her the גט works from now. So if he dies at night, this is clearly just a condition, and it is a גט given during his life. This follows רב הונא, who said: anyone who says 'on condition' is like one who says 'from now'.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a second wording where everyone agrees, but this time the גט is valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'On condition' does not delay the start of the גט; it starts now, and the condition only has to be met later. Once the sun rises, the condition is met, and the גט counts from the moment it was given, while he was alive. רב הונא's rule is the source for reading 'on condition' as 'from now'.

keyTerms.meaning: A גט that takes effect while the husband is alive

steps.confusionAlert: 'When the sun comes out' and 'on condition that the sun comes out' sound almost the same, but they work opposite ways. 'When' delays the start of the גט, while 'on condition' starts it now, with a condition attached.

phrases.english: If he said 'On condition that the sun comes out of its sheath,'
he is telling her it works from now,
and if he dies during the night,
this is certainly just a condition,
and it is a divorce given while he was alive,
in line with Rav Huna,
as Rav Huna said:
Anyone who says 'on condition'
is like one who says 'from now'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues אביי's list with a second wording, where everyone agrees the opposite way.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'On condition' wording makes the גט start now, so it is valid even if he dies before the condition is met, following רב הונא.

steps.title: The real argument: the wording 'if the sun comes out'
steps.stepSummary: The argument is only about 'if the sun comes out'. רבי יהודה הנשיא follows רבי יוסי, so the date on the גט makes it count from that day, and it is valid. The חכמים reject רבי יוסי, so it is a plain 'if I die' גט, which is invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: They only argued about 'if the sun comes out'. רבי יהודה הנשיא holds like רבי יוסי, who says the date of a document shows when it takes effect. So it is like saying 'from today if I die' or 'from now if I die'. The חכמים do not hold like רבי יוסי, so it is just a plain 'this is your גט if I die'.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי now pinpoints the one wording where רבי יהודה הנשיא and the חכמים argue. He explains that their argument depends on רבי יוסי's rule about dates on documents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'if' does not say clearly whether the גט starts now or later. For רבי יוסי, the date written on the גט shows that it starts from that date, which turns it into a 'from now' גט, valid while the husband was alive. The חכמים do not use the date this way, so the גט starts only later, after his death, and it fails.

keyTerms.meaning: The date of a document shows when it takes effect

steps.whatToRemember: Three wordings: 'when' means a גט after death, invalid according to everyone. 'On condition' means 'from now', valid according to everyone (רב הונא). 'If' is the argument: רבי יהודה הנשיא, following רבי יוסי, uses the date to make it 'from now' and valid, while the חכמים treat it as a plain 'if I die' and invalid.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the court's lenient ruling from steps 12-14. It also explains why the חכמים disagreed: everything depends on whether we accept רבי יוסי's rule about the date on a document.

phrases.english: They only disagreed about 'if it comes out,'
phrases.notes: 'They' are רבי יהודה הנשיא and the חכמים from step 14.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הַנָּשִׂיא סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi holds like Rabbi Yosei,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: זְמַנּוֹ שֶׁל שְׁטָר מוֹכִיחַ עָלָיו,
phrases.english: who says: the date of a document proves when it takes effect,
so it is like saying 'from today if I die,'
or like 'from now if I die,'
and the Rabbis do not hold like Rabbi Yosei,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָוֵה לֵיהּ כְּ״זֶה גִּיטִּיךְ אִם מַתִּי״ גְּרֵידָא.
phrases.english: so it is like a plain 'this is your divorce if I die.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's three-part list by identifying the one disputed wording and the reason behind the dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With 'if' wording, רבי יהודה הנשיא, following רבי יוסי, makes the גט valid based on its date, while the חכמים rule it is a plain 'if I die' גט and invalid.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The disagreement between רבי יהודה הנשיא and the חכמים is limited to 'if' wording and depends on רבי יוסי's rule about the date on a document.

steps.title: Returning to the testimony of יוסי בן יועזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings back the full text of יוסי בן יועזר's testimony about three cases, and his nickname 'יוסף שריא', 'the Permissive.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the main text: יוסי בן יועזר from צרידה testified that the איל קמצא is kosher, that the liquids of the slaughterhouse are pure, and that one who touches a dead body is impure. People called him 'יוסף שריא', 'the Permissive.'
steps.whatsHappening: The word גופא tells us the גמרא is returning to a source it mentioned earlier so it can study that source on its own. This step quotes the source and sets up the questions that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יוסי בן יועזר testified about three rulings, and each one was more lenient than people expected. Because he ruled leniently so often, he got the nickname 'שריא,' the one who permits. The rest of the sugya will explain each of his rulings, starting with the איל קמצא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The thing itself.' The גמרא is returning to study a source it quoted earlier
Testified. He passed on a ruling he had received
A type of locust. Its identity is discussed next
The liquids of the slaughterhouse in the בית המקדש
The one who permits, the lenient one

phrases.english: The matter itself:

phrases.aramaic: הֵעִיד יוֹסֵי בֶּן יוֹעֶזֶר אִישׁ צְרֵידָה
phrases.english: Yosei ben Yo'ezer of Tzereida testified
about the eil kamtza, that it is kosher,
and about the liquids of the slaughterhouse, that they are pure,
and about one who touches a dead body, that he is impure,
and they called him 'Yosef the Permissive.'
phrases.notes: Yes, his name was יוסי, but the nickname uses the form יוסף.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא: הֵעִיד יוֹסֵי בֶּן יוֹעֶזֶר אִישׁ צְרֵידָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of conditional גיטין and goes back to examine the testimony of יוסי בן יועזר on its own.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The איל קמצא is kosher, the slaughterhouse liquids are pure, and one who touches a dead body is impure.

steps.title: What is the איל קמצא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which creature the איל קמצא is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the איל קמצא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple question to define a term from the testimony. This sets up the two answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We cannot understand why יוסי בן יועזר's ruling counted as lenient until we know which creature he was talking about. This is a question about the meaning of a word, not an attack on his ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: What is? Used here to ask what a term means

phrases.english: What is the eil kamtza?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the first item in the testimony.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which kind of locust the איל קמצא is.

steps.title: Two identifications of the איל קמצא
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the איל קמצא is the שושיבא. רב חייא בר אמי, quoting עולא, says it is the סוסביל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said it is the שושיבא. רב חייא בר אמי said in the name of עולא that it is the סוסביל.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give different answers to the question of which locust the איל קמצא is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each answer names a different kind of locust. Because they picked different creatures, each view will explain differently why יוסי בן יועזר's ruling was lenient. The גמרא explains each one next.

keyTerms.meaning: A kind of locust with a long head
In the name of. Quoting an earlier teacher

phrases.english: Rav Pappa says: a shoshiva,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב חִיָּיא בַּר אַמֵּי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּעוּלָּא
phrases.english: and Rav Ḥiyya bar Ami, in the name of Ulla,
says: a susbil.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of what the איל קמצא is.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Two answers: the שושיבא according to רב פפא, and the סוסביל according to עולא.

steps.title: For רב פפא, the argument is about a long-headed locust
steps.stepSummary: According to רב פפא, יוסי בן יועזר and the other Sages argue about whether a locust with a long head is kosher. The גמרא then starts to give עולא's explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said it is the שושיבא, and they argue about a locust with a long head. One Sage holds that a long-headed locust is forbidden, and the other holds that it is permitted. רב חייא בר אמי said in the name of עולא:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the argument is about if we follow רב פפא. Then it opens with רב חייא בר אמי's name to set up עולא's explanation, which continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שושיבא has a long head. Some Sages thought a long head means the locust is not kosher, while יוסי בן יועזר permitted it. That is why his ruling counted as lenient.

keyTerms.meaning: They argue. This tells us what the disagreement is about
Its head is long. The feature in question

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'מר... ומר' does not name the two sides. Following the context, the forbidding opinion belongs to the other Sages and the permitting one belongs to יוסי בן יועזר.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa says: a shoshiva,
and they argue about a locust whose head is long.
One Sage holds: a long-headed one is forbidden,
and the other Sage holds: a long-headed one is permitted.

phrases.aramaic: רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אַמֵּי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּעוּלָּא אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Ḥiyya bar Ami says in the name of Ulla:

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: שׁוֹשִׁיבָא, וְקָמִיפַּלְגִי בְּרֹאשׁוֹ אָרוֹךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains what the argument is about if we follow רב פפא's answer, then begins עולא's explanation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב פפא, the argument is whether a long-headed locust is kosher. יוסי בן יועזר permitted it.
